items.title: [The Guardian Global Development] Rats, dengue and an all-day stench: can Panama City solve its waste crisis?
items.content_html:
For decades, mountains of waste have blighted poor neighbourhoods on the edge of the city. But as the problems spread, a belated reckoning is under way

Life in San Miguelito has long been dictated by rubbish. Routes to the shop are carefully navigated to avoid pungent mountains of rotting waste, some visible from space. Driving during the rainy season is a perilous obstacle course, dodging black bin bags and rusty fridges in the middle of the road. Children are taught early to avoid the river, the rubbish, the rats, yet mosquito-borne diseases still stalk the community.

For Yamileth, who lives with her family on one of the steep, narrow streets that thread the hillside neighbourhood, the waste is a constant backdrop to daily life. Mornings are punctuated by the stench and buzz of flies, and in the evenings you can hear rats scuttling and stray dogs rustling as they rip open bags in search of food among the rubbish heaps, known in slang as patacones (also the name of a staple side dish made from green plantains).

items.title: [ScienceDaily] Earth's fiery birth may have created hundreds of oceans' worth of water
items.content_html: Earth's water may have been born in the planet's fiery atmosphere rather than delivered by icy comets or asteroids. Scientists discovered that rocky pebbles reacting with hydrogen under extreme heat can produce water in minutes, potentially generating hundreds of oceans' worth during Earth's formation. The findings suggest that water may be a natural part of how rocky planets form, rather than something that must arrive from space.

items.title: [space.com] SpaceX prepares Starship Flight 15 for first attempt to catch both stages
items.content_html: SpaceX moved Super Heavy Booster 22 to the launch mount at its Starbase facility in South Texas on Nov. 10 ahead of a Nov. 13 Starship test flight that will attempt to catch both the booster and the Ship upper stage with the launch tower’s mechanical arms. The 75-minute launch window is scheduled to open at 4:45 p.m. local time, subject to regulatory approval. The booster is due to return about 6½ minutes after liftoff; Ship is scheduled to return roughly 22 hours later after deploying 26 Starlink V3 satellites and completing about 14 orbits. SpaceX has caught Super Heavy boosters three times but has never attempted to catch Ship, which must re-enter from orbit. The company will proceed with Ship’s return only if its systems meet the flight team’s criteria; otherwise, it plans an ocean landing.

items.title: [cbsnews.com] US charges three men over alleged Iran-linked UK airbase plot
items.content_html: The U.S. Justice Department charged three men on Nov. 10 over an alleged plot to attack RAF Fairford, a British air base used by U.S. forces, and their alleged involvement in other attacks. The defendants are Mohammad Baqer Saad Dawood al-Saadi, a dual Iranian-Iraqi national; Mohsen Mohajeri, an Iranian national; and Mohammad Ali al-Hassani, an Iraqi national. Prosecutors allege they acted in support of Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and the Iraqi armed group Kata'ib Hezbollah. The eight-count indictment says al-Hassani organized British associates, arranged for vans carrying fuel and made other preparations, while al-Saadi sent coded messages through relatives from a New York jail. Prosecutors allege the vans were meant to explode at the base; British police found no explosives but seized fuel. Only al-Saadi is in U.S. custody; prosecutors have not disclosed the other two men’s whereabouts. The indictment also links the defendants to nearly 20 alleged attacks or attempted attacks against Jewish communities and other targets in Europe and North America. The U.S. withdrew its B-1 bombers from Fairford after the September incident; Iran has denied involvement.

items.title: [cnbc.com] France summons Iran envoy and seeks EU sanctions over supermarket hack
items.content_html: France summoned Iran’s ambassador on Nov. 10 and said it would seek European Union sanctions and consider other responses to a cyberattack on supermarket refrigeration systems that Paris attributes to Iran’s Revolutionary Guard. The October operation affected about 700 French retail sites. Tehran has denied responsibility. French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said Paris would take measures it considered proportionate to deter further attacks, including steps it would not disclose publicly. The Paris prosecutor’s office opened a judicial investigation into the Shahid Kaveh cyber unit and requested international arrest warrants for its leader and two deputies. Iran’s Foreign Ministry called the accusation baseless and one-sided, while Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi accused France of shifting blame. The EU said it was ready to coordinate a response with member states. Foreign ministers are due to discuss the issue on Nov. 16.

items.title: [orf.at] Drone strikes kill two power-plant workers near Ukraine’s occupied nuclear site
items.content_html:
🔧 ✏️

Drone strikes killed an employee of the Russian-occupied Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant and a worker at a nearby thermal power station on Monday, Nov. 9, the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) said. The agency did not say who carried out the attacks. Moscow-appointed plant management blamed Ukrainian forces for the nuclear-plant worker’s death, while Russia and Ukraine have repeatedly accused each other of attacks around the site. The nuclear plant’s six reactors have been shut down since 2022, but safety systems still require electricity. On Nov. 8, the plant lost its sole 330-kilovolt external power line for about 10 hours and used emergency diesel generators for cooling and other safety functions until power returned. The IAEA has maintained a presence at the facility since September 2022. The latest deaths followed the reported killing of another plant employee in a drone attack on Oct. 29. IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi condemned the attacks and called for them to stop. The agency has not publicly assigned responsibility for the strikes.

items.content_html: President Donald Trump said on Nov. 8 that renewed U.S. strikes on Iran were “highly unlikely” if negotiations produce a strong agreement on Tehran’s nuclear program and reopening the Strait of Hormuz, while warning that U.S. forces remain ready to attack. He said the military had identified 38 bridges as potential targets. The conflict, now in its ninth month, remains at a stalemate, with shipping incidents continuing around the strait. U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Washington was not close to a diplomatic breakthrough and called Iran’s demands unacceptable. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said mediators had stopped traveling after the Nov. 3 U.S. midterm elections. He reiterated Tehran’s offer to reopen the strait within two days if Washington meets its conditions, including ending the war on all fronts. U.S. Central Command has established a roughly 20-person task force to disrupt routes carrying weapons and sanctioned goods across Iran’s land borders and the Caspian Sea, expanding U.S. efforts beyond its naval blockade. Trump is scheduled to meet Qatar’s prime minister on Monday, Nov. 9, as Doha continues mediation.

items.title: [libertatea.ro] Poland declares mourning after Kraków shooting kills six, injures foreigners
items.content_html: Poland began two days of national mourning on Sunday, Nov. 8, while Kraków declared mourning through Nov. 11, after a gunman killed six people and wounded at least 15 in the city’s historic Main Market Square on Saturday. The Polish suspect drove through the square firing at passersby before police shot and arrested him. One of those killed was British, and five injured foreign nationals were from Austria, Germany, Portugal, Russia and Britain. Kraków recorded 16.2 million visitors in 2025, according to the city. Police cordoned off the historic centre, and city officials urged residents and tourists to avoid the area while the investigation continued. Gunfire also shattered a window in a tram driver’s cabin, but no passengers were hurt. Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński said early findings suggested the suspect was influenced by far-right ideologies, a possibility investigators would examine. Authorities were also investigating three bodies found at the suspect’s home in Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski; Prime Minister Donald Tusk said there were strong indications they were members of the suspect’s immediate family.

Activists fear Bangkok will give in to pressure from Beijing despite reports of torture and human rights abuses against the mostly muslim ethnic minority

The deportation of two more Uyghurs to China from Thailand would put their lives in grave danger, activists have said, with one of the men saying he would be “like a slave” if he was sent back.

Last year, Thai authorities forcibly deported 40 Uyghur men to China despite pleas from the men themselves and the UN.

The US and Canada had reportedly offered to resettle them, but Bangkok appeared to want to avoid upsetting Beijing. The UN has said the returnees’ whereabouts remain unknown.

items.title: [cbc.ca] Parks Canada expects to eliminate about 500 full-time-equivalent positions, ends Banff rescue-dog program
items.content_html:
🎨 🌾 🪶 ✏️

Parks Canada expects to eliminate about 500 full-time-equivalent positions, close 13 park-warden detachments and discontinue its Banff search-and-rescue dog program as part of $145 million in cuts over three years. The agency sent workforce-adjustment notices to 2,917 employees and says it will make individual decisions in the coming weeks. The Canadian Avalanche Rescue Dog Association and British Columbia Search Dog Association have urged the agency to reverse the cancellation, warning it could weaken rescue capacity. Parks Canada says it will shift wardens to a regional model focused on high-risk areas and that wardens can enforce park law without dogs. The associations say they are working on a short-term volunteer response during avalanche season.
